<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video in which almost nothing happens, on purpose.</b><br>
  <sub>Working title. In development. An unofficial remake inspired by <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 desert-island screensaver.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="tools/serve.py"><b>run it</b></a> &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <a href="activities.toml">the schedule</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <a href="tools/make_audio.py">the sound</a> &nbsp;·&nbsp;
  <a href="MUSING.md">the notes</a>
</p>

One tiny island, one tall palm, one raft, one young woman in cream headphones, and a lot of time. She idles, nodding to the music, and every so often something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A shark in headphones nods along. A coconut falls on a hermit crab, and the crab leaves wearing it. It is a stationary-frame video for YouTube in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, sunny hand-painted coastal anime, and always daytime.

The screen up there keeps score the arcade way. Gags are points. Headphones are lives, and the drone is the extra life. There are no controls, because there is nothing to do: in a typical ten-hour run she is busy about a third of the time and idle for the rest, and the idle is the point.

More than 90 activities live in [activities.toml](activities.toml), on four timers: something regular every 2 to 5 minutes, occasional every 12 to 25, rare every 30 to 60, and super rare every 3 to 6 hours. Lanes let them overlap, and every one waits for the next bar of the music (every 3 seconds), so the punchlines land on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, mixed to -14 LUFS. Nobody has listened to it yet. It is extremely well measured.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

Live preview in the page, then export a YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes frame-exact H.264 with WebCodecs, and the server mixes in the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm. [`python tools/schedule.py`](tools/schedule.py) checks the schedule and simulates a ten-hour run; [`python tools/render_demo.py --dev`](tools/render_demo.py) renders a dev reel of every activity. Nothing is published yet, so for now the only way to watch her do nothing for ten hours is to run it yourself.

<details>
<summary><b>XY MODE</b>: the theme, drawn as one green line</summary>
<br>
<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/72-vector-beam-display_opus_5.5-scope.svg" width="100%" alt="An oscilloscope screen with a green graticule. One closed green trace draws the theme's four chords, one bar each, as Lissajous figures that drift and then morph on the bar line: Gm9 and Dm9 as 6:5, root against minor third; C13 and Fmaj9 as 5:4, root against major third. Beside it, a sand-coloured now-playing readout: NOW PLAYING, THE THEME, 60 S LOOP. 80 BPM, F MAJOR, 20 BARS OF 3 S, II-V-I-VI. Four chord boxes, Gm9, C13, Fmaj9 and Dm9, the current one lit. X: ROOT, Y: the current third and its ratio. E-PIANO, KALIMBA, SOFT DRUMS, VINYL CRACKLE. EVERY SOUND SYNTHESIZED FROM CODE. NO SAMPLES. In dim letters: DRAWN FROM THE CHORD NAMES, NOT FROM THE FILE. HEARD SO FAR BY: NOBODY.">
</p>

On an XY scope the left channel moves the beam sideways and the right channel moves it up and down, so a sound draws its own picture. A silent README cannot do that honestly, so this one cheats in the open: the four chords are the ones [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py) plays, one per 3-second bar (Gm9, C13, Fmaj9, Dm9, a ii-V-I-vi in F), and each is drawn as its root against its third, rounded to the nearest small ratio so the figure closes. The real file sounds like whatever it sounds like. Nobody knows yet.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>DIP SWITCHES</b>: the four timers, factory settings</summary>

```text
 ┌─ SLOWBEAM 72 · OPERATOR DIP SWITCHES · FACTORY SETTINGS ────────────────┐
 │                                                                         │
 │  BANK  TIMER         COMES ROUND EVERY   PER 10-HOUR RUN   1 2 3 4 5 6  │
 │  ────  ────────────  ──────────────────  ────────────────  ───────────  │
 │   A    regular       2 to 5 minutes      about 155         ▀ ▄ ▀ ▀ ▄ ▀  │
 │   B    occasional    12 to 25 minutes    about 30          ▄ ▀ ▀ ▄ ▀ ▄  │
 │   C    rare          30 to 60 minutes    about 13          ▀ ▀ ▄ ▄ ▀ ▀  │
 │   D    super rare    3 to 6 hours        about 2 (max 3)   ▄ ▄ ▄ ▄ ▄ ▀  │
 │   E    chained       never on a timer    follow-ups        ▄ ▀ ▄ ▀ ▄ ▀  │
 │                                                                         │
 │  START ON ......... the next bar (every 3 s, 80 BPM)                    │
 │  LANES ............ overlap allowed (a ship may pass while she is       │
 │                     busy; it usually does)                              │
 │  BUSY ............. about a third of the time                           │
 │  RUN .............. 10:00:00                                            │
 │  SEED ............. 1992                                                │
 │  FREE PLAY ........ always (there is no play)                           │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Counts are the median of 200 simulated ten-hour runs, as the file's own header says. The chained bank is the follow-ups: the tide that comes for the sandcastle, and the like. Rebalancing the timers is on the list for later; for now the occasional bank is crowded and some of its gags wait a long time for their turn.

</details>

<summary><b>ATTRACT MODE</b>: the banner's minute, bar by bar</summary>

```text
 BAR  TIME   STATUS LINE                   WHAT THE BEAM DRAWS
 ───  ─────  ────────────────────────────  ────────────────────────────────
 01   00:00  ALL QUIET ON THE ISLAND       the title, redrawn stroke by
                                           stroke; a plane crosses
 03   00:06  BOTTLE AWAY                   she throws; it lands; it drifts
 05   00:12  BOTTLE BACK. NO REPLY YET     it washes straight back to her
 08   00:21  ALL QUIET                     nodding, on every beat
 09   00:24  DRONE INBOUND                 a parcel, lowered on a line
 11   00:30  EXTRA LIFE: MORE HEADPHONES   the parcel pops; lives 2 -> 3
 13   00:36  SHARK IN RANGE                a fin in headphones, circling
 15   00:42  SHARK NODS ON THE BEAT        80 nods a minute; the parcel
                                           floats off with the tide
 17   00:48  INCOMING COCONUT              bonk
 18   00:51  CRAB LEAVES IN NEW HAT        it walks into the sea, hat on
 20   00:57  ALL QUIET AGAIN               the title decays to a ghost,
                                           the coconut grows back
```

The real video spaces these out by minutes or hours. The banner crams an unusually eventful evening into one minute, which is also the length of the theme, so the whole screen loops when the music would.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>SERVICE MANUAL</b>: how the screen is drawn</summary>

**No pixels.** The banner is one SVG, made by a Node script with no dependencies. Every line is a stroke drawn three times, a wide faint halo, a mid glow and a thin near-white core, so it glows without a blur filter. The lettering is an original stroke alphabet (a few straight segments per letter, chamfered corners), drawn as paths so it looks the same for every viewer.

**The overlay.** The beam is white. The colour comes from three tinted rectangles laid over the tube with a multiply blend, the way a plastic overlay sheet works: coral over the title strip, aqua over the island, sand over the status line. Anything that crosses a boundary changes colour there; the headphones do, on their way up to the lives counter.

**The island.** A 3D wireframe (sand contours, the palm with bark rings and fishbone fronds, two rocks, some bushes, a five-log raft) on a slow turntable, 26 degrees each way, once a minute. It is projected at 16 keyframes and played back as one path morph with eased timing, so the sway has no corners. She, the parcel and the crab are flat cut-outs that ride the same turntable. The real video never moves its camera, so somebody had to.

**The sea.** Fifteen broken swell lines roll towards you, one arriving per bar. Each line's shape depends only on how far away it is, so the loop has no seam.

**The title.** Its ghost is always on screen, so the name reads from the first frame. At the top of every minute the beam redraws the front face stroke by stroke, with a spark where each stroke ends, holds it with a faint shimmer, and lets it fade back to the ghost in the order it was drawn. Twice a minute the whole tube dims for a single frame, as busy vector screens did.

**Reduced motion.** With reduced motion switched on, the screen holds still on a complete first frame: title lit, island at rest, status reading ALL QUIET ON THE ISLAND.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>GREETINGS FROM THE BEAM</b></summary>
<br>

To the island regulars: the sea turtle, who visits; the stray cat (grey tabby, white chest), who arrives on a crate, naps up the palm and one day floats off again, and then comes back; the bro on the electric hydrofoil (shaka received); the tour boat of selfie-takers; the shark, for wearing headphones correctly; the hermit crab, for wearing a coconut with dignity; the kumara, growing as fast as it can; and the ship, which as usual waited until she was busy.

To the vector arcade cabinets and home vector consoles of 1979 to 1984, and to the people who make music that draws pictures on oscilloscopes: credited here as the inspiration for the look. Nothing of theirs is copied; the alphabet, the island and the overlay are all drawn from scratch. SLOWBEAM is made up, like the score.

</details>
